title: feat(plugin-calendar): declare the `sort` input both `object-calendar` registrations read
body:
Fixes #8171

objectui#7712's defect, one key over. ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove, resolved toward **declare** — plus the ledger rider objectui#8212 left for whichever of the two landed second.

## What changed

- One `inputs` entry, `type: 'array'`, on each of the two registrations that publish `ObjectCalendarRenderer` — `plugin-calendar:object-calendar` and `view:calendar`.
- The `sort` row the plugin docs page omitted (objectui#7070), mirroring the `filter` row objectui#8186 added.
- The declaration pin, extended in place.
- **The rider** — see below.

## Ordering: objectui#8212 has LANDED, and this PR carries the rider

⚠️ This section replaces an earlier account written before that happened; a reader should not have to reconstruct it from comments.

objectui#8212 landed as `cf2bd3722` and widened `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` to judge the lazily-registered `object-calendar` / `object-kanban` blocks. The PM ruled ordering **B**: that change first, this one carrying the rider — because the gate file's own rule is that declaring an input turns it RED until the covering entry is deleted **in the same change**, and this is the change that declares `sort`. `origin/main` was merged in (merge, never rebase — the branch was already pushed).

Measured on the merged tree, before the rider: **3 failed / 195 passed of 198**, all three naming `object-calendar.sort` — `carries no stale unpublished-key exemption`, `judges a non-vacuous member-shape census`, and `object-calendar pins the member shape of every array/object input it declares`. After: **198 passed / 198**.

⭐ The assertion count does not move — 198 both ways. All three edits are ledger **data** consumed by assertions that already existed; the rider adds no `it()` to this gate. The new assertions live in the pin file instead (`plugin-calendar` goes 26 files / 161 tests to 27 / 167).

## The rider — three edits

1. **Deleted** `object-calendar.sort` from `UNPUBLISHED_EXEMPTIONS`. Its own text says objectui#8171 owns the declaration and its landing deletes the entry; a declaration retires its own cover, the documented exit the two `filter` entries took under objectui#8186. Left a tombstone in its place, in the idiom the file already uses.
2. **Lowered the shrink-only objectui#8176 backlog ceiling, 16 to 15.** ⚠️ **Correction to the brief this seat was given:** that ceiling is carried by **two** assertions in the same `it`, not one — `toBeLessThanOrEqual(16)` (the may-not-grow ceiling) and `toBe(16)` (the exact measured size). Only the second reddens on its own, so a change that lowered only the exact one would leave a unit of headroom banked — precisely what the surrounding comment says the ratchet exists to refuse ("rather than banking the headroom their fixes free up"). Both are now 15.
3. **Added a `MEMBER_PINS` entry**, not a member-pin exemption. `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING` is untouched at **62**, and `the ceiling correction admits exactly the four keys objectui#8176 made visible` still names its four by name.

## ⛔ The member pin is NOT an identity pin — objectui#8212's rider note predicted the wrong shape

That note (now replaced by the tombstone) said: "`sort` is the same kind of pass-through key (`ObjectCalendar.tsx` hands it to the query), so the member claim is the same identity-forwarding one." **Measured, that is false**, and the same prediction was relayed to this seat in its brief, so it is corrected in three places (the tombstone, the changeset, and here).

`ObjectCalendar.tsx:479` writes `$orderby: convertSortToQueryParams(schema.sort)`. That sink **builds a new value** — a `field` to `direction` map — so the authored array never reaches the wire. `toBe` on `$orderby` is false about this key and could not have passed at any point in this file's history. (Independently corroborated by a test already on main: `ObjectCalendar.elementDataSource.test.tsx` asserts `params.$orderby` `toEqual({ name: 'desc' })` for an authored `[{ field: 'name', order: 'desc' }]`.)

The difference makes the member claim **sharper, not weaker**. `filter`'s members are opaque to this renderer, so its pin says *nothing is read inside*. `sort`'s members **are** read, so this pin says exactly what is read:

`packages/plugin-calendar/src/__tests__/ObjectCalendar.sortMembersReachTheWire-8171.test.tsx`, six rows:

1. `{ field, order }` lowers to the `field` to `direction` map.
2. An omitted `order` is **ascending**, not a dropped member — the objectui#4022 regression, which is member-level and invisible to every other direction of the parity gate.
3. Every member arrives, in authored order (per-member, not first-wins).
4. A member with no usable `field` is **dropped, never given an invented one** — the negative half of row 1, which is what makes `field` *read* rather than merely carried.
5. objectui#7711's core case transposed: a sort on a field literally named `calendar` (this block's own configuration container) stays a sort, and the config still comes from the declared `calendar` key — asserted through the rendered event titles, so a member read as configuration would show up as a refusal screen or a mis-placed event.
6. **The control** — an unauthored `sort` reaches the wire as `undefined`, not as a fabricated default, with `$top > 0` as the non-vacuity check so `undefined` is a verdict about `$orderby` rather than a read of an empty parameter object.

The spec cannot supply any of this: the `sort` row is unconstrained (measured on `@objectstack/spec` 17.2.0 — an array, a bare string and a bare number all parse), so the wire is the whole member contract. Same reasoning both `filter` entries record.

## The card's original measurements, re-run

The card measured `9bfd618`; objectui#8186 (`0ead1f62a`) landed into this file in between. Measured versus claimed:

| card claimed | measured | drift |
|---|---|---|
| `ObjectCalendar.tsx:479` reads `$orderby: convertSortToQueryParams(schema.sort)`, deps at `:514` | both exact | none |
| `index.tsx:67` — `OBJECT_CALENDAR_DATA_SOURCE` asserts `sort: true` | at `:65` | 2 lines up |
| the two registrations' `inputs` are `objectName` and `calendar`, no `sort` | each list now carries a third entry, `filter`, from objectui#8186; still no `sort` | the omission is unchanged, the neighbourhood is not |
| the spec accepts an authored `sort`, undeclared key refused by name on the same call | reproduced: `success: true`, empty `unrecognized_keys`, `bogusProp` refused by name | none |

⚠️ `OBJECT_CALENDAR_DATA_SOURCE` was read and deliberately **not** used as the source of the declaration — it is an `ElementDataSourceMapping`, not an inputs list, and objectui#7712 measured what a mechanical derivation from it costs (kanban's `limit`, which the spec refuses by name). The `type: 'array'` arm is convention, verified rather than assumed: all seven `sort` declarations in the tree write it, against a 39-hit `objectName` control.

## Clause-② — the authoring face does widen, and why it should clear

`needs:contract-review` is attached, with the reviewable increment in hand rather than prospectively. The widening is real: a key `validateTree` reports as `unknown-prop` today stops being reported. The grounds, stated rather than assumed — the same ones objectui#8186 cleared on:

- **The spec already declares the key**, measured with the refusal control on the same call, so the save gate already lets it through.
- **The renderer already honours it** (`ObjectCalendar.tsx:479`).

Both ends are already live, so this restores `declared = enforced` on the tier in the middle rather than widening past the contract. What it removes is objectui#6678's shape, where the one spelling that WORKS drew the same diagnostic as a write that does nothing.

## ⛔ This still does not make the next omission loud

`check:react-blocks-declaration-parity` runs manifest to spec, one direction, so a spec-declared key the manifest omits is outside what it ratchets. Fixing this key does not close the class; that is #8176. (Unchanged by objectui#8212, which widened the console's own parity gate, a different instrument.)

## Tests

All on the final commit, `ced8a7904` (content unchanged by the merge above it).

- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts packages/plugin-calendar/` — **28 files, 365 tests, all passed** (198 parity + 167 calendar). Run from the repo root throughout; the `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run FILE` form objectui#3378 guards against was never used.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-calendar type-check` exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the pins are type-checked, not excluded).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check` exit 0 — ⚠️ only after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/console^...' build`. Its first run failed with nine `TS2307` / `TS2882` module-not-found errors from unbuilt workspace `dist`, none of them in the edited file; that run is reported as NOT MEASURED, not as red.
- `check:sdui-registration-pins` — **now green** (`All 16 registration(s) ... present in the built console (518 chunks weighed)`), measured after `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build`. An upgrade from the first round, which could only report it as NOT MEASURED.
- Gates, exit codes captured by redirect-then-capture, never through a pipe: `check:control-bytes` 0 (6576 files) · `check:element-data-source-declaration` 0 · `check:doc-fences` 0 · `check:doc-types` 0 · `check-changeset-presence` 0 · `check-changeset-no-major` 0 · `check:governed-queue-guard --test` NOT GOVERNED.
- Still declared to CI: `check:doc-snippets` (exit 2 pending a 34-package build; the only doc edit is one line inside a `plaintext` fence, and `doc-fences` / `doc-types` both pass on it), and the affected consumer packages.

### Ablation of the NEW member pin — it can fail, and reddens by name

Renderer mutated at the line the pin's subject reads (the pin imports `../ObjectCalendar` relatively, so the source file is what runs — no `dist` hop, and none claimed). Each mutation proven to reach disk by an anchored `grep -cxF` count of both the canonical and the mutant line, before and after; each restore proven **BY STATE** (`git hash-object` equal to `git rev-parse HEAD:PATH` **and** `git diff HEAD` empty), never by an exit code; `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths.

| leg | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | none | 6 passed |
| 1 | `$orderby: schema.sort` — i.e. make it the pass-through objectui#8212's note predicted | **5 failed / 1 passed.** The only survivor is the CONTROL row, exactly as designed. The pin refuses that false claim by construction. |
| 2 | drop members carrying no `order` — the objectui#4022 regression, surgically | **1 failed / 5 passed**, and it is the right one BY NAME: `reads an omitted 'order' as ascending instead of dropping the member`, `AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { starts_at: 'asc' }`. |

### Ablation of the declaration pin — per registration, not per file

Unchanged from the first round: dropping `sort` from the `object-calendar` registration alone reddens exactly its two rows while both `view:calendar` rows stay green, and vice versa; flipping one entry's arm to `type: 'object'` reddens only that registration's arm row.

## Note for the PM, not an action request

While this branch was being pushed, another actor merged `main` into it remotely (`3de5b5964`, "Merge branch 'main' into ...") — under the shared identity there is no way to tell which seat. Its tree is byte-identical to this seat's own merge of the same commit. ⛔ Not force-pushed and not reverted; it was merged in and pushed on top, so nothing of theirs is lost.

## Out of scope, filed separately

Dedup-searched first, with a control query in the same session returning known-present cards.

- **#8220** — `object-map`, `object-gantt` and `object-timeline` lower BOTH `filter` and `sort` while none of their six registrations declares either. ⚠️ Filed with the difference stated: those three tags are absent from `ComponentPropsMap` entirely, so the spec argument this card rests on is unavailable and it is NOT a mechanical repeat.
- **#8221** — the legacy string `sort` clause `convertSortToQueryParams` honours is declared by none of the seven `sort` inputs, so the html tier answers `type-mismatch` for a spelling core documents. Surfaced by this change, not caused by it.

⛔ Kanban's `limit` untouched — measured NEGATIVE, and it is #8172, `needs-user-decision`. ⛔ `packages/plugin-kanban` untouched.

This PR stays a **DRAFT** — the PM lands it. Not flipped ready, no auto-merge. Generated by an agent seat via Claude Code, session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`.
